proof:
# Exact Tukey facets need not have finite active cap certificates

Take n=2,d=1 and

`C=[0,1]^2 x [0,1]`, `S={0,1}^2 x [0,1]`.

Unnormalized mixed volume is M=4; let mu be its normalization to probability.
Let D_tau be the full ambient Tukey region of depth at least tau=1/5, and
let P_tau be its projection to the two integer-coordinate axes.

## Exact constrained and boundary depths

For any point on an integer fiber, an oblique halfspace can isolate that
fiber and cut its interval at the selected point, keeping its shorter side.
Thus every point of S has depth at most `(1/2)/4=1/8`. At the midpoint of
any fiber every containing halfspace keeps at least half that fiber, so
`max_{y in S} depth_mu(y)=1/8` exactly. Therefore P_tau contains no integer
point.

Consider instead the unconstrained point

`y_0=(0,1/2,1/2)`.

The two fibers with first integer coordinate zero have total mass 1/2 and
are centrally symmetric about y_0. Every closed halfspace containing y_0
therefore contains at least mass 1/4. The halfspace
`x-L z_1>=1/2`, for L>=1, has exactly mass 1/4 and contains y_0. Hence

`depth_mu(y_0)=1/4 > tau`.

More generally, at `y_t=(0,t,1/2)`, 0<=t<=1, the exact depth is

`depth_mu(y_t)=1/[8 max(t,1-t)]`.

To verify it, first restrict any halfspace to the two fibers z_1=0. Reflection
in x=1/2 reduces to inequalities
`x>=1/2-r(z_2-t)`. Their unnormalized retained lengths sum to

`clip(1/2-r t,0,1)+clip(1/2+r(1-t),0,1)`.

A piecewise-linear minimization in r gives `1/[2 max(t,1-t)]`.
Every such restricted cut can be extended with a sufficiently large negative
z_1 coefficient to exclude the other two fibers. Division by M=4 proves
the formula.

Consequently the supporting face of P_tau on z_1=0 contains the nontrivial
segment `3/8<=z_2<=5/8`. The four edge-midpoint projections all belong to
P_tau, so P_tau is full-dimensional. Since D_tau is contained in conv(S),
P_tau is contained in [0,1]^2. Thus z_1=0 is an actual flat supporting facet.
The maximal lattice-free split `[0,1] x R` contains P_tau and has this facet
contact.

## No finite mass-tau cap Farkas certificate for this facet

Let H_i be ANY finite collection of closed ambient halfspaces with
`mu(H_i)<=tau`. Since y_0 has depth strictly larger than tau, it lies
strictly outside every H_i. Therefore it strictly satisfies all complementary
closed halfspace inequalities.

Every nonzero finite nonnegative combination of these inequalities is also
strict at y_0. It cannot equal the supporting inequality `-z_1<=0`, which is
tight at y_0. Equivalently, every finite intersection of such complementary
halfspaces contains an ambient neighborhood of y_0, whereas D_tau does not.

This does not contradict ordinary Farkas' lemma: the exact Tukey region is
an INFINITE intersection, and its supporting inequality here comes from
limits of cap inequalities. In the limiting vertical halfspace, whole
integer fibers can carry boundary mass. The limiting closed cap can have
mass greater than tau.

The example obstructs a general claim of finitely many attained mass-tau
active caps at every exact vertical facet contact. It does not assert an OC
counterexample: its chosen level tau=1/5 exceeds the sharp OC level 1/8.
Any argument restricted to hypothetical below-OC counterexamples would need
to prove a new property excluding this boundary phenomenon, rather than
assuming ordinary finite active-set calculus applies.
